clue.text: Closest to Solomon Islands, going in one direction

indicators.note: going in tells us the islands abbreviation is placed inside the compass word

parts.note: west is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: Someone asks which Pacific islands lie nearest to the Solomons when heading one way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solomon Islands' reads as the Pacific nation, but Solomon is the biblical king famed for wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: King Solomon is the byword for wisdom, so whoever comes nearest to him in that quality is the most sage.

clue.text: Like film that's worth seeing with a companion after getting food round

indicators.note: round means the food word goes around the companion abbreviation

parts.note: table means food served, as in keeping a good table
CH stands for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A movie that deserves viewing if you go with a friend after picking up something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order; food as 'table' is the sense of keeping a good table.
explanation.definitionFit: A film worth seeing is one that can be viewed with pleasure, the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Pan prepared to receive what you've bagged?

indicators.note: to receive means the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: set means prepared or ready
a kill is the game a hunter has bagged

explanation.surface: A frying pan stands ready for whatever the hunter brings home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what you've bagged' sounds like shopping, but it is a hunter's kill.
explanation.definitionFit: A skillet is a heavy frying pan, so it is one kind of pan.

clue.text: Leave radio with no reception

parts.note: a radio is a wireless set
a radio that is off receives nothing

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a radio that cannot pick up a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off is to depart or begin a journey, a phrasal synonym for leave.

clue.text: Envied fellow, one who wore drainpipes?

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a chap or fellow
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth who wore narrow drainpipe trousers

explanation.surface: Someone envied a man who once dressed in narrow trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were a 1950s British youth fashion: long jackets, drainpipe trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are past-tense verbs meaning wanted what belonged to another; a straight synonym.

clue.text: A walk in the park at top of Coney Island

indicators.note: at top of means the first letter, the top in a down answer

parts.note: inch is a Scottish word for a small island

explanation.surface: A stroll through the amusement park on Coney Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A walk in the park' suggests the New York resort but means something easy. INCH is a Scottish word for an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal idioms for a task that is very easy to do.

clue.text: Holidaymakers on sunny climb through northern half of Vosges

indicators.note: through means the reversed words run inside the half-word
northern half means the top half of the word in a down answer
climb means the words read upwards, so backwards in a down answer

parts.note: re means on or about
gay in its old sense means cheerful or sunny

explanation.surface: Tourists in good spirits hike up into the hills of the Vosges mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climb' turns RE + GAY into YAGER, which goes 'through' VOS, the top half of Vosges.
explanation.definitionFit: Voyagers are travellers on a journey, which loosely covers people on holiday trips.

clue.text: Cuckold standing up to wife during broadcast

indicators.note: during means one letter sits within the short word

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: standing up means the word reads upwards, backwards in a down answer

parts.note: emit means broadcast or send out

explanation.surface: A deceived husband stands up to his wife while on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckold' is here a verb, to be unfaithful to a partner, not the deceived husband the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To cuckold is to be unfaithful to one's partner, the same act as deceiving them with another.

clue.text: Material, greenish on the inside, dark outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for dark wraps around the middle letters

parts.note: dim means dark or poorly lit

indicators.note: on the inside means the central letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: A fabric with a green interior and dark exterior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the inside' takes the middle two letters of greenish; the colour words are only surface dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a sturdy cotton twill fabric, so it is a material.

clue.text: Heard hearse, perhaps, approaching part of cemetery in foreign city

indicators.note: heard means the pieces are said aloud to give a similar-sounding name

parts.words: hearse, perhaps, approaching part of cemetery
parts.note: a hearse is an example of a car, and a tomb is part of a cemetery, so this says car tomb

explanation.surface: Mourners hear the hearse drawing near the graveyard in a city abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, car tomb approximates the name of Sudan's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Khartoum is the capital of Sudan, a city abroad from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: One wanting more bread

parts.note: Dickens's orphan Oliver famously asked for more food in the workhouse; bread also hints at money

explanation.surface: A person hungry for an extra slice, or for extra cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver, the workhouse boy in Dickens's novel, holds out his bowl and asks for more; bread is both food and slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel's title character is the most famous literary figure ever to beg for a second helping.

clue.text: Precious little time available for romantic break

parts.note: honey is a term of endearment, like precious or darling
a mo is a moment, a short while
on means available, as a dish that is on the menu

explanation.surface: A couple find they have barely any free time for a loving getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precious' looks like an adjective modifying 'little', but it is a noun of affection.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday taken by newlyweds straight after the wedding is the archetypal romantic trip away.

clue.text: Captured stronghold close to Edinburgh and declaimed

parts.note: held means captured or seized
a fort is a fortified stronghold

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An army took the fortress near Edinburgh and then made a speech about it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means spoke at length and pompously, the same as orated grandly.

clue.text: Ghastly male writer

parts.note: grim means ghastly or horrible

explanation.surface: A frightful man who writes.
explanation.walkthrough: The brothers Grimm collected German fairy tales, fittingly ghastly ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob and Wilhelm, the fairy-tale collecting brothers, are writers known by this surname.

clue.text: Bible originally in Greek

parts.note: the first letter of Bible is B, and the Greek alphabet's equivalent of B is its second letter

explanation.surface: A remark that the scriptures were first written in Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the New Testament's original language; the cryptic sense is the initial letter of Bible rendered as its Greek counterpart.
explanation.definitionFit: The second letter of the Greek alphabet corresponds to the Roman letter B.

clue.text: Dam with water supply for Scottish town

parts.note: a dam is a mother, especially of an animal
a well supplies water

explanation.surface: A reservoir with its own source of water is planned for a Scottish place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dam' suggests a reservoir wall, but it is the word for an animal's mother. MOTHERWELL is a town in Lanarkshire, Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Motherwell is an industrial town south-east of Glasgow, so it is an example of a Scottish town.

clue.text: Produced with craftsmanship, assistant reported

indicators.note: reported means the word is spoken and we take a word sounding the same

parts.note: a handmaid is a female servant or assistant

explanation.surface: A craftsman's helper says the work was made skilfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods made by hand rather than machine are produced with an artisan's skill.

clue.text: Painting wins international award: fame at last!

parts.note: lands means wins or secures, as in lands a contract
a cap is a selection to play for one's country, an international

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of the word before

explanation.surface: An artwork takes a major global prize, and its painter is finally famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'international award' suggests a prize, but CAP is a sporting international, a player chosen for the national side.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a picture of countryside scenery, a kind of painting.

clue.text: Failing energy: extremely serious condition of advancing age?

indicators.note: failing suggests the letters of energy break down and reform
extremely means the first and last letters of the following word

explanation.surface: Loss of vigour and a grave illness are signs of growing old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing' shuffles ENERGY, and 'extremely' takes SS, the ends of serious. The question mark flags that grey hair is only one sign of ageing.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair turning grey is a familiar mark of getting older, so the state is linked to ageing.

clue.text: Boffin secures explosive mine in scientific investigation

indicators.note: secures means holds fast within, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a boffin is British slang for a scientific expert

indicators.note: explosive suggests the letters of mine are blown apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A scientist handles a live mine during a research project.
explanation.walkthrough: A boffin is British slang for a scientist or expert; 'explosive' looks like a description of the mine but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A controlled test carried out to discover something is the classic scientific procedure.

clue.text: Model with a bit of clothing on coming under pressure

indicators.note: coming under means the following pieces sit below the pressure letter in a down answer

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
a rag is a scrap of cloth or garment
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fashion model wearing a scrap of fabric feels pressured.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'coming under' puts A RAG ON beneath P.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a perfect example to follow, a model of some quality.

clue.text: Hide most of bust

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: skint is British slang for bust, meaning broke

explanation.surface: Someone tells you to conceal nearly all of a statue's head and shoulders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the final T of SKINT, British slang for penniless. 'bust' suggests a sculpture, but means broke.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's hide is its skin, both nouns for the outer covering.

clue.text: Expression of alarm turning up at fish bar

indicators.note: turning up means the word reads upwards, backwards in a down answer

parts.note: eek is a cry of fright
a pout is a kind of fish, also called a bib

explanation.surface: Someone shrieks in alarm on arriving at a fish restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a place serving fish but is a verb, to forbid entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar someone is to stop them entering, the same as keeping them away.

clue.text: Queen received by man of God briefly in place of worship

indicators.note: received by means the queen abbreviation is taken inside the other word
briefly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Moses is the biblical prophet, a man of God

explanation.surface: A queen is welcomed by a cleric during a short visit to a temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man of God' suggests a priest, but here it is the biblical prophet, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosque is a building where Muslims pray, a place of worship.

clue.text: Railway line doubles back at first, causing concern

indicators.note: at first places the turned piece before the railway abbreviation
doubles back means the word for line is turned round

parts.note: a row is a line

explanation.surface: A railway track that loops back on itself is a source of anxiety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubles back' turns ROW into WOR, and 'at first' puts that ahead of RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken as a verb, to fret is to be a cause of anxiety, so the sense is troubling or concerning.

clue.text: Vowel shift partly evident in language

indicators.note: partly evident in says the answer can be seen as a run of letters inside the words before

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A linguist notes a change in vowel sounds that shows up in a language.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'evident in language' as the definition, but only 'language' can stand for the answer; 'partly evident in' is the hiding signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh is the Celtic tongue of Wales, so it is an example of a language.

clue.text: Scout gatherings monarch admits are without interest

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the monarch's name holds the other piece

parts.note: James is the name of several English and Scottish kings
to bore is to be dull, without interest to others

explanation.surface: A king lets in some youngsters' get-togethers, though they are tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are without interest' reads as a comment on the gatherings, but it is the verb meaning to be tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large rally of Scouts or Guides, so the plural is Scout gatherings.

clue.text: Provocatively interesting description of ripe oranges

definitions.meaning: spicy or racy, as with scandalous gossip
ripe oranges are full of liquid

explanation.definitionFit: Racy gossip is called succulent, and ripe citrus fruit is full of liquid; both senses fit the word.

clue.text: Turning idle, hang back to begin with?

definitions.text: Turning idle, hang back to begin with?

indicators.note: turning means the letters are spun around into a new order
to begin with means the first letter of the word before

explanation.surface: A lazy person asks whether their idleness started with dawdling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' shuffles IDLE and HANG with B, the opening of 'back' signalled by 'to begin with'. The whole clue also defines: going idle is to hang back.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail or fall behind others is the same as hanging back, which is what an idler does.

clue.text: 50% of one Oxford dictionary's contents: acceptable amount

indicators.note: 50% of means half of the word is taken, the opening half

parts.note: the Oxford Dictionary of Quotations is full of quotations

explanation.surface: Someone estimates that half an Oxford dictionary's entries is a reasonable amount to read.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oxford Dictionary of Quotations is one Oxford dictionary; its contents, QUOTATIONS, has ten letters, and the first five are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A quota is a fixed share or allowance, the permitted amount of something.

clue.text: Wren's accommodation on board sailing vessel has open feature

indicators.note: on board means carried within the vessel, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a hoy is a small coastal sailing vessel
a wren, the small bird, lives in a nest

explanation.surface: A naval servicewoman's cabin on a ship has an open aspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wren' suggests a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service, apt on board, but it is the bird. HONESTY is also a plant, so 'feature' of an open character.
explanation.definitionFit: Being open and candid is a character trait, and frankness is that trait.

clue.text: Pay for piece of furniture

definitions.meaning: to pay a bill is to clear it
a long wooden bench with a high back and arms

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means pay off a debt, and the noun is a high-backed wooden bench seat.
